title: AEOeye vs AthenaHQ: One-Off Audit or Monthly Monitoring?
metaTitle: AEOeye vs AthenaHQ: Which Should You Use? (2026)
metaDescription: AEOeye vs AthenaHQ: a $0–$29 one-off AI visibility audit against a $295/month credit-metered platform. Who should pick which, with prices as of October 2026.
shortAnswer: Pick AEOeye if you need a one-time answer to "do AI engines name us, and who do they name instead?": the free audit asks ChatGPT three buyer questions, and a $29 one-time report covers ten questions on five engines. Pick AthenaHQ if you will review a prompt list every week and act on it: Starter is $295 a month, metered in credits.
intro:
This comparison is based on AthenaHQ's public documentation and pricing pages as of October 2026; we have not tested the product hands-on. AEOeye is our product, so weigh our opinions with that in mind. Every fact about AthenaHQ below comes from [its own pricing page](https://athenahq.ai/plans) or [homepage](https://athenahq.ai/).

Older versions of this page, and plenty of others, framed this as free versus paid. That framing is out of date: AthenaHQ now has a Free plan with 300 credits. The real difference is what you are buying. AEOeye sells a snapshot; AthenaHQ sells an instrument you run every week.

sections.heading: Which should you choose, AEOeye or AthenaHQ?
sections.body:
Choose by the question you need answered. If it is "are we invisible in AI answers?", a one-time audit settles it for $0 to $29. If it is "is our share of those answers rising, and what should we publish next?", you need continuous tracking, and AthenaHQ is built for that.

**Choose AEOeye if:**

- You have never looked at what ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity say when buyers ask about your category.
- You want a fixed price with no subscription and no credits to forecast.
- You (or your agency) will act on the findings without a dashboard.

**Choose AthenaHQ if:**

- Someone owns AI visibility as a weekly channel and has a prompt list worth tracking.
- You need Google Analytics, Search Console or Shopify connected, or enterprise controls such as SSO.
- You want monitoring and content recommendations in one product.

Our position: take the snapshot first. A tracker pointed at the wrong prompts measures the wrong thing, and the audit tells you which questions and competitors matter. The exception is a team that already knows it has a problem and has budget: for them, AthenaHQ's Free plan is a cheaper first step than our report.

sections.heading: What is each tool built for?
sections.body:
AthenaHQ is a monitoring-and-action platform for [generative engine optimization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_engine_optimization), the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by AI systems. AEOeye is a diagnostic: it tells you where you stand today and what to fix first.

AthenaHQ's [homepage](https://athenahq.ai/) describes three layers: monitoring across 11+ models, action tools with on-page and off-page recommendations, and a content agent. It lists integrations with GA4, Google Search Console, Shopify, Webflow and Framer. It also runs an [agency program](https://athenahq.ai/agency) with multi-brand client management and discounted licenses.

AEOeye does one job. The free audit asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions and shows the real answers in full, plus the competitors named instead. The $29 one-time report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity, ten questions instead of three, a five-layer SEO foundation audit and a fix roadmap. We test each engine at the default tier a free user gets, not a stronger one.

What AEOeye is not: a daily tracker, a content writer, or a promise that engines will recommend you.

![Three colleagues planning and brainstorming with laptops in a bright modern office](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8511930/pexels-photo-8511930.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do pricing and coverage compare?
sections.body:
AthenaHQ meters usage in credits; AEOeye sells one report. On [AthenaHQ's pricing page](https://athenahq.ai/plans), 1 credit equals 1 AI response, and Starter costs $295 a month for 3,600 credits. That implies about $0.082 per response. AEOeye's $29 report covers 50 question-and-engine answers, about $0.58 each.

On raw volume, AthenaHQ is roughly seven times cheaper per response. That comparison is unfair to both sides, though: our report is a one-time diagnosis with a roadmap, not a metered feed, and you pay once instead of every month. The table below sets the two side by side.

Credits also hide a sampling question. AthenaHQ's [credit calculator](https://athenahq.ai/credit-calculator) estimates usage from "prompts, locations, models, and cadence". In a study of 2,961 runs, [SparkToro and Gumshoe found](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/) a less than 1-in-100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI returns the same brand list twice, and suggested asking at least 60 to 100 times and averaging.

By our arithmetic, 3,600 credits at 60 responses per prompt-and-model pair covers 60 pairs a month. We do not know how AthenaHQ samples, so ask how many responses it collects per prompt before you trust one number. The same caution applies to us: our audit takes one sample per question and engine, so read it as a diagnosis, not a score to chase.

sections.heading: Where is AthenaHQ stronger?
sections.body:
AthenaHQ wins on breadth, continuity and workflow. If you will use those, it is the better product for you, and we would say so even if you never paid us.

- **Coverage:** Starter lists 11 models, including AI Mode, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and Mistral, per its [plans page](https://athenahq.ai/plans). Our report covers five engines.
- **Continuity:** it re-checks prompts over time, so you can see a trend. We give you one dated snapshot.
- **Connections:** GA4, Search Console, Shopify and Webflow tie AI visibility to site traffic, per its [homepage](https://athenahq.ai/).
- **Action layer:** content recommendations and an agent sit next to the data. We hand you a roadmap and stop there.
- **Team features:** unlimited seats on every plan, and SAML SSO, multi-region support and BI dashboards on the quote-only Enterprise tier.
- **A real free plan:** $25 of free credit, described as 300 credits, across five platforms. That is a sanity check on a handful of prompts, not trend tracking.

sections.heading: Where is AEOeye stronger?
sections.body:
AEOeye wins when cost certainty and speed matter more than depth. You get a complete answer to one question, once, at a price you know in advance.

- **No meter:** $0 for the ChatGPT audit, $29 once for the five-engine report. Nothing renews.
- **Real answers, shown in full:** you read what each engine actually said to a buyer-style question, and which competitors it named instead.
- **Default-tier testing:** we do not use stronger models than your buyers see.
- **Site basics included:** the report adds a five-layer SEO foundation audit, so crawlability and structure problems are on the same page as the visibility gap.

Why a baseline matters: in AEOeye's own audit records (127 audits, 27 distinct brands, June to September 2026), brands were named in 157 of 892 answers, or 17.6%. That sample is small and self-selected, and per-engine rates are not comparable, so treat it as a reminder that being named is the hard part. The [method and caveats are here](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement).

sections.heading: What did we see on each vendor's own site?
sections.body:
In AEOeye's crawler access study (October 2026), neither site blocks AI bots. This is a neutral fact box about how each presents itself to machines, not a verdict on either product.

- **athenahq.ai:** robots.txt blocks no AI bots and names none explicitly. It publishes an llms.txt. The served homepage HTML had no JSON-LD, which can mean the schema is injected by JavaScript rather than absent.
- **aeoeye.com:** robots.txt blocks no AI bots and names six explicitly (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended). It publishes an llms.txt, and the homepage carries Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication with Offer, and FAQPage markup.

Method and limits (one fetch per site, one day) are in our [crawler study notes](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory). For a longer, documentation-based read of the product, see our [AthenaHQ guide](/blog/athenahq-review), the other [AthenaHQ alternatives](/alternatives/athenahq), or the wider [AI visibility tool comparison](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools).

keyTakeaways: AthenaHQ now has a Free plan (300 credits), so the old free-versus-paid framing is outdated: the real split is snapshot versus monitoring.
AthenaHQ Starter is $295 a month for 3,600 credits, where 1 credit equals 1 AI response; extra credits and API access have no published price.
AEOeye's free audit is ChatGPT-only (3 questions); the $29 one-time report adds four engines and ten questions.
AthenaHQ is stronger on coverage (11 models), trends, integrations and workflow; AEOeye is stronger on fixed cost and speed to a first answer.
Take the snapshot first unless you already know you have a problem and a team to act on weekly data.

faqs.q: Does AthenaHQ have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes, as of October 2026. Its pricing page lists a Free plan with $25 of free credit, described as 300 credits, covering ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini and Copilot. Starter is $295 a month. We have not used the product, so this comes from its public pricing page.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a replacement for AthenaHQ?
faqs.a: No. AEOeye is a one-time audit: a free three-question ChatGPT check and a $29 report across five engines. It does not re-check prompts daily or weekly, and it does not write content. If you need ongoing monitoring, AthenaHQ or another dedicated tracker fits better.

faqs.q: How much does AthenaHQ cost per month?
faqs.a: Starter is $295 a month for 3,600 credits, with 1 credit equal to 1 AI response, as of 3 October 2026. Annual billing is labeled 17% off. Extra credits and API access are paid add-ons with no published price, and Enterprise is a custom quote.

faqs.q: Which AI engines does each tool cover?
faqs.a: AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT only; the $29 report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity. AthenaHQ's Free plan lists five platforms and Starter lists 11 models, including AI Mode, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and Mistral. Both lists come from public pages as of October 2026, and we have not tested either product's coverage ourselves.

faqs.q: Should I run an audit before paying for monitoring?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A snapshot shows which buyer questions and competitors matter, so you track the right prompts from day one. If you already know you have a gap and a team to act on weekly data, starting on AthenaHQ's Free plan is a reasonable shortcut.
